# HLT-C9 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: McCullough JM, Eisen-Cohen E, Lott B (2020). Barriers and facilitators to intraorganizational collaboration in public health: Relational coordination across public health services targeting individuals and populations. Health Care Management Review 45(1), 60-72. doi:10.1097/HMR.0000000000000203.

Text: JSTOR copy supplied by the author (PDF page 1 is a JSTOR cover sheet), converted with pdftotext -layout to _text/HLT-C9.txt. Page references use the journal pagination (printed p.60 = PDF page 2; printed page n = PDF page n - 58).

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- Object: collaboration (relational coordination) among the 18 services of the Maricopa County Department of Public Health (MCDPH), Arizona, "the only local governmental entity that provides public health services in this jurisdiction" (p.62).
- Relationships studied: coordination between services within one public organisation (shared goals, shared knowledge, mutual respect, communication; p.61-62), and barriers and facilitators to it (p.64-69).
- Public service: governmental local public health department; per capita expenditure reported (p.62).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: relational coordination survey of the senior representative of all 18 services (7 items, 1-5 scale; p.62-63); ANOVA and t tests; overall mean 3.15, significant variation by service focus (p < .001), domain scores (p.63-64, Figure 1, Table 2).
- Qualitative: 17 semistructured key informant interviews, open and axial coding (p.63); four facilitator themes and four barrier themes (p.64-69, Tables 3-4).
- The study describes itself as a "convergent mixed-methods design" (p.62) and links survey and interview responses at service level (p.63).

## Notes
- Joint claims were not used as a criterion (author decision, 17 November 2026).
- The PDF text layer renders "<" as "G" and em dashes as "V"; quotes in the register restore the symbols.
